text:
Maya: heads-up, ran into an ambiguous match in the gateway when host capture patterns, a header-anchor and a service alias all exist for the same request.
Maya: minimal example: 
```yaml
- match: host: '*.example.com' -> service: svc-v1
- match: host: 'api.example.com' path_prefix: '/v1/' -> service: svc-v2
- match: header:X-Target: 'payments' -> service_alias: payments-svc
```
Maya: request to api.example.com/v1/payments with `X-Target: payments` — which rule should win? feels foggy.
Liam: agreed this is messy. my gut: deterministic specificity order + explicit anchors. propose: 1) exact host+path 2) host capture with path specificity 3) header anchors 4) service_alias fallback. i.e. header anchors are a weaker tie-breaker than explicit host/path.
Liam: tiebreaker between two host captures = longest literal prefix -> then lexicographic.
Sanjay: curious about why header anchors are weaker — headers are explicitly set by client, seems like a stronger signal in some cases (eg tenant routing).
Maya: true. tradeoff is accidental header injection vs url-based routing. for internal tenants we do want header to win sometimes.
Tess: UX idea: console should show the match trace for the request (exact rule matched + fallback chain + why others lost). small panel next to route eval. :eyes:
Tess: also suggest we add a `match_priority` numeric field in route config so ops can override defaults for edge cases.
Liam: +1 to `match_priority` but keep default computed by the server so most configs stay simple. priority only for explicit overrides.
Sanjay: also think metrics/labels need to reflect the final chosen "route_id" and the "candidate_rules" so we can monitor ambiguous hotspots.
Maya: could we also surface a debug header when `debug=true` param present: `X-Gateway-Match-Trace: id=svc-v2;matched=host_path;losers=[header_anchor:payments]` for quick traces?
Tess: we already have a lightweight `X-GW-Route` header in staging. exposing a richer `X-GW-MATCH` for debug mode is fine but should be gated.
deploy-bot: prod deploy scheduled: gateway/matcher-refactor -> canary at 05:30 UTC; will include match_priority and trace header behind feature flag.
Maya: ok i'll open a short RFC capturing: default precedence, numeric override, console match-trace UI, metrics labels, and debug header.
Liam: i'll draft the RFC and include sample evaluation matrix + unit tests (requests matrix).
Sanjay: add test for header-injection attempt to ensure security logic doesn't let arbitrary header wins unless explicit priority set.
Maya: thanks — adding checklist to RFC: config syntax, precedence table, console wireframe, metric labels, unit & integration tests, rollout plan with FF.
Liam: cool, ping me when draft is up @Maya. :+1:
